# tools: command: transcribe — speech to text with MacWhisper by default

## Motivation

Turn a recording into text with one command that scripts and coding agents can call as easily as a human, without remembering engine flags. In practice MacWhisper's bundled CLI `mw` with the Parakeet v3 model is fast, accurate for Russian and separates speakers, so it is the empirical default; the choice of model is traded for that default, with an escape hatch for the rare override. The previous `transcribe` and `whisper` shell functions (Whisper `small` in Docker, 2023) were not used and are removed; a shell function must not shadow the new command.

`mw` lives inside the app bundle (`/Applications/MacWhisper.app/Contents/MacOS/mw`, since MacWhisper 13.20). It reaches `PATH` through the in-app installer (`/usr/local/bin/mw`, admin password, removed only from the app's settings) or, once accepted, through the cask's `binary` stanza (Homebrew/homebrew-cask#303304).

## PoC

```bash
$ transcribe call.m4a > call.txt                     # text to stdout, Unix way
$ transcribe call.m4a -o call.srt --format srt       # a file only when asked
$ transcribe a.m4a b.m4a --output-dir notes/          # several inputs
$ transcribe call.m4a --names "Pavel,Kamil"           # Speaker 1/2 → names, in order of appearance
$ transcribe call.m4a -- --model whisperkit:openai_whisper-large-v3-v20240930   # engine args as is
transcribe: engine mw (parakeet-pro:nvidia_parakeet-v3), language ru               # on stderr
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bin/transcribe` is on `PATH` for login shells, scripts and agents; no function or alias named `transcribe` or `whisper` remains in `bin/lib`.
- [ ] Defaults: engine `mw`, model `parakeet-pro:nvidia_parakeet-v3`, language `ru`, speaker detection on, grouping by people, timestamps, format `txt`; never `--persist` (nothing lands in MacWhisper's history).
- [ ] Output goes to stdout; `-o <file>` and `--output-dir <dir>` write files and refuse to overwrite without `--force`; several inputs require `--output-dir`.
- [ ] Own flags stay few: `--lang`, `--format txt|srt|vtt|md|json`, `--names`, `--engine`, `-o`, `--output-dir`, `--force`; everything after `--` reaches the engine unchanged, and a flag given there replaces the matching default instead of being passed twice.
- [ ] `--names` relabels `Speaker N` in order of appearance in text formats; more speakers than names keep their generic labels.
- [ ] The engine is found as `mw` on `PATH`, else inside `/Applications` or `~/Applications`; the chosen engine and model are reported on stderr, the transcript alone on stdout.
- [ ] `--engine` is a seam for more engines (an on-device macOS transcription API when Apple ships one); with one engine today, `auto` means `mw`.
- [ ] Exit codes: 0 success, 1 engine failure, 2 usage error, 127 no engine found, with a hint how to get `mw`.
- [ ] bats tests with a stub engine cover argument pass-through (spaces included), defaults replaced by pass-through, `--names`, refusal to overwrite, missing engine, and stdout/stderr separation.

## Out of scope

Installing MacWhisper or `mw` (Brewfile and the cask PR cover that); choosing or downloading models; post-processing such as summaries; a second engine — only the seam for it; the agent skill that decides to save a transcript next to its source when no post-processing is asked.
